### Workflow entry: urlshort-slice-delegated-b@1 step requirements

Workflow instance: 01M4170AA9E72WW1BXEA5PX0AP
Entry step: requirements (requirements)

Root objective: Mission 02-brownfield, slice 02-click-retention (OPR.99.0.3.2, tier low, delegated plan-lock to the lead under D11, wave w1 with 01-audit-read; QA by qa2-agent, review by review2-agent, proof judge qa2-agent per slice.yaml). Intent: An Operator can rely on clicks older than the retention period (90 days by default, an operator setting) being deleted on schedule, so click data stops growing without bound and no visit is kept longer than decided. Human's mission plan-lock (2026-10-03T15:40Z, verbatim): approve: three slices in two waves as briefed, with the four labelled drills; purge stays here with the 90-day default as an operator setting. Requirements: NFR-P2 (90 days, decided at mission 01's plan-lock), FR-13 (existing links and statistics unchanged), NFR-X2 for any migration. Design hint from decompose: delete by the stored UTC click day (clicked_on), the period an operator setting, so mission 03's retention answer changes a number, not this slice. BROWNFIELD: design writes impact-analysis.md over the shipped click table and statistics (missions/01-greenfield-core/slices/02-analytics, merged 091ff46; ADR-0011..0013) before design.md. ORDERED CUSTODY in w1: this slice is the SECOND holder of src/main/resources/application.properties and the Flyway V number; its implement step hands off a candidate that descends from 01-audit-read's merge commit (rebase onto main after that merge; the integrator checks git merge-base --is-ancestor before merging); if the build is otherwise done first, exit waiting --blocked-on 01-audit-read's frontier packet with the continuation rebase onto main, take the next V number, hand off. Territory: click/ main, unit, functional; db/migration only if the purge needs an index; application.properties for the retention setting; not link/, audit/, web/, docs/api/openapi.json. FR-15 in passing (mission 01 wave review W2-05): a click reduction failure reports reason rejected, which the design defines only as a full or closed queue; widen that definition or use a distinct static reason, no new logging layer. Tests: a 90-day purge test will shift FunctionalClock, so its shifted requests must come from a dedicated peer address (the rate limiter keeps that peer's bucket after reset; see FunctionalClock.shift Javadoc and mission 01 NOTES section 2 12:40Z). Cross-mission: mission 03's 01-analytics-v2 also touches click/; it is at requirements now and its plan-lock orders it against this slice. Queue order on the requirements seat: 01-analytics-v2 first, then 01-audit-read, then this slice. Worktree .worktrees/02-click-retention on slice/02-click-retention from main f6dd29e (product = 8e9c065). Read first: missions/02-brownfield/SPEC.md, its NOTES.md, this slice's slice.yaml and SPEC.md scaffold.

Step objective: Write the slice SPEC.md: user stories, GIVEN/WHEN/THEN acceptance criteria, business rules, scope, ambiguity log, proof contract. Park a real ambiguity on the human; otherwise record safe defaults.
